title: Symmetric Functions, the Hall Inner Product, and Schur Bases

items.title: The stable graded ring of symmetric functions
items.statement: For d≥0 set Λ^d=lim←_N Z[x_1,…,x_N]^{S_N}_d under x_{N+1}=0, and Λ=⊕_{d≥0}Λ^d with multiplication induced by finite projections. Λ is not the ungraded inverse limit of the finite symmetric-polynomial rings.
items.proof_strategy: Define each transition on the homogeneous degree-d part, including N=0 and d=0. Verify compatibility of products under specialization, then take the direct sum so every element has finite degree support. Explain that the ordinary inverse limit also contains inhomogeneous infinite-degree sequences such as ∏_i(1+x_i), which are excluded here.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: Skew diagrams and semistandard skew tableaux
items.statement: For μ⊆λ in English convention, [λ/μ]=[λ]∖[μ]. A semistandard skew tableau fills these boxes by positive integers, weakly increasing along rows and strictly down columns; its weight records multiplicities. A horizontal strip has at most one box in each column. Edge-connected components share sides.
items.proof_strategy: Use inherited English row and column indexing and its semistandard inequalities, now restricted to pairs of boxes present in the skew diagram. Define the empty skew diagram and its unique empty filling; only partitions with μ⊆λ carry a skew diagram.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I

items.title: The monomial symmetric functions form the integral stable basis
items.statement: For every d≥0, the stable orbit sums m_λ, indexed by partitions λ⊢d, form a Z-basis of Λ^d.
items.proof_strategy: Pad λ by zeros at rank N. The published finite orbit-sum theorem supplies an integral basis in every rank. For N≥d, every partition of d has length≤N and the specialization from N+1 to N sends each corresponding orbit sum bijectively to the same label; hence the transition is an isomorphism. Transport that basis through the degree-d inverse limit, including d=0.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: Stable Schur functions from bialternants
items.statement: For λ a partition and N≥ℓ(λ), with δ_N=(N−1,…,0), define s_λ(x_1,…,x_N)=det(x_i^{λ_j+N-j})/det(x_i^{N-j}). For 0≤N<ℓ(λ), define the component to be zero. These compatible components define s_λ∈Λ^{|λ|}, including s_∅=1 at every rank.
items.proof_strategy: The pairwise nonassociate prime variable differences divide the alternating numerator, so their Vandermonde product divides it and the quotient is integral and symmetric. Above the length boundary, specialize the last variable to zero and cancel the common product of remaining variables. At the boundary, the numerator has a zero last row while the denominator specializes to a nonzero polynomial; the polynomial identity forces the quotient specialization to zero. Below the boundary both components are zero. Empty determinants give the constant unit sequence.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: Bidegree completion of two symmetric-function rings
items.statement: Define the completed bidegree tensor ring Λ(x)⊗̂Λ(y)=∏_{a,b≥0}(Λ^a(x)⊗_ZΛ^b(y)), with multiplication by finite convolution in each bidegree. The Cauchy kernel belongs to the diagonal components (d,d).
items.proof_strategy: For a fixed output bidegree (a,b), only finitely many decompositions (a,b)=(i,j)+(a−i,b−j) occur, so convolution is well defined and associative. Distinguish this completion from Λ itself and from the ordinary ungraded inverse limit.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: Elementary and complete families freely generate the stable ring
items.statement: Λ=Z[e_1,e_2,…]=Z[h_1,h_2,…], each family is algebraically independent, and {e_λ:λ⊢d} and {h_λ:λ⊢d} are integral bases of Λ^d.
items.proof_strategy: In each degree, expand e_{λ′} in the monomial basis. A squarefree factorization gives only m_μ with λ⊒μ; the coefficient of m_λ is one, so the matrix is dominance-unitriangular over Z. Hence e_λ is an integral basis and the e_r are freely algebraically independent. Pass the published finite-variable identity H(t)E(−t)=1 to stable degrees; its recurrence makes the substitution e_r↔h_r triangular with unit diagonal in both directions, proving the same claims for h.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: Jacobi–Trudi and dual Jacobi–Trudi identities
items.statement: For every partition λ, s_λ=det(h_{λ_i−i+j})_{1≤i,j≤r}=det(e_{λ′_i−i+j})_{1≤i,j≤c}, where r≥ℓ(λ), c≥ℓ(λ′), h_0=e_0=1 and negative-index terms vanish.
items.proof_strategy: At finite rank N, derive H_N(t)=∏(1−x_it)^{-1} and use H_N(t)∏_{l≠k}(1−x_lt)=(1−x_kt)^{-1}. Coefficient extraction gives A_α=H_αM; δ_N identifies det M with the Vandermonde, and α=λ+δ_N gives the h determinant. Prove padding by a zero part leaves either determinant unchanged and pass every rank component to Λ. For the dual formula lift E(−t)H(t)=1 coefficientwise, build inverse upper Toeplitz matrices, and prove the needed complementary-minor block identity over Frac(Λ), with the beta-set complements and permutation/entry signs explicit. Treat λ=empty directly and state negative indices as zero.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: Power sums form a rational but not integral stable basis
items.statement: After scalar extension, Λ_Q=Q[p_1,p_2,…] with {p_λ:λ⊢d} a Q-basis in degree d. The p_λ are not generally a Z-basis of Λ^d.
items.proof_strategy: Define stable p_r by the compatible finite-rank sequences and set Λ_Q=Q⊗_ZΛ. At each finite rank derive H_N(t)=∏_{i=1}^N(1−x_it)^{-1} from the complete-homogeneous definition, then H_N′/H_N=Σ_{r≥1}p_r^{(N)}t^{r−1}. Pass coefficientwise through the stable inverse limit to obtain Newton recurrence n h_n=Σ_{r=1}^n p_rh_{n-r}. Its mutually inverse triangular substitutions between p_n and h_n over Q give the rational polynomial basis. At degree two, h_2=(p_1^2+p_2)/2 has nonintegral coordinates in the p-basis, disproving integral spanning.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: The Hall inner product on symmetric functions
items.statement: The Hall form is the graded Z-bilinear pairing on Λ with ⟨h_λ,m_μ⟩=δ_{λμ} for partitions of equal size and orthogonality across unequal degrees.
items.proof_strategy: In each stable degree, the proven h and m integral bases make the displayed dual-basis rule a unique bilinear form. Pair unequal degrees by zero and extend over the algebraic direct sum; only finitely many degree components contribute. Later Cauchy identities derive symmetry and the Schur orthonormality result.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: The omega involution conjugates Schur functions
items.statement: There is a graded integral ring involution ω with ω(e_r)=h_r, ω(h_r)=e_r, ω(p_r)=(-1)^{r−1}p_r over Q, and ω(s_λ)=s_{λ′}.
items.proof_strategy: Use the stable finite-rank logarithmic-derivative identity to obtain tH′/H=Σ p_rt^r coefficientwise in Λ_Q[[t]]. Define ω from the free e generators, and use the coefficient recurrence of E(−t)H(t)=1 to prove ω(h_r)=e_r and ω²=1. Apply ω to the h Jacobi–Trudi determinant and use the dual formula for λ′ to get ω(s_λ)=s_{λ′}. Apply ω to the H logarithmic derivative, compute tE′/E from the finite product, and compare coefficients to get ω(p_r)=(−1)^{r−1}p_r.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: Power-sum, complete, and Schur expansions of the Cauchy kernel
items.statement: In Λ(x)⊗̂Λ(y), Ω=∏_{i,j}(1−x_i y_j)^{-1}=Σ_λ h_λ(x)m_λ(y)=Σ_λ s_λ(x)s_λ(y). In the componentwise rational completion ∏_{a,b}(Λ_Q^a(x)⊗_QΛ_Q^b(y)), Ω also equals Σ_λ z_λ^{-1}p_λ(x)p_λ(y), where m_r(λ)=#{i:λ_i=r} and z_λ=∏_{r≥1}r^{m_r(λ)}m_r(λ)!. All sums are by bidegree (d,d).
items.proof_strategy: For the h/m expansion, expand each finite geometric product in the y variables and group exponent vectors into distinct monomial orbits. For the p expansion, derive log Ω=Σ_{r≥1}p_r(x)p_r(y)/r coefficientwise from finite products in the rational bidegree completion, then expand the exponential by multiplicities to obtain z_λ. For the Schur expansion, prove the finite Cauchy double-alternant identity by divisibility and variable-degree bounds, determine its constant from the lowest-degree Cauchy–Binet term, expand the determinant into pairs of alternants, divide by the two Vandermondes, and pass each bidegree to the stable completion. No proof-only result from a prerequisite, analytic convergence, or Hall self-duality is used.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: Power sums are orthogonal for the Hall form
items.statement: In Λ_Q, ⟨p_λ,p_μ⟩=δ_{λμ}z_λ, with z_λ=∏_{r≥1}r^{m_r(λ)}m_r(λ)!; unequal degrees are orthogonal.
items.proof_strategy: In each degree, compare Ω_d=Σ h_ν(x)m_ν(y) with Ω_d=Σ p_ν(x)(p_ν(y)/z_ν). A finite change-of-basis matrix and its inverse transpose show that the two factors in any such kernel expansion are dual for the Hall form. Thus p_ν and p_ν/z_ν are dual; use the rational p basis and grade orthogonality to obtain the formula.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: Schur functions form an orthonormal integral basis
items.statement: For every d≥0, {s_λ:λ⊢d} is a Z-basis of Λ^d and ⟨s_λ,s_μ⟩=δ_{λμ}.
items.proof_strategy: Expand the h Jacobi–Trudi determinant: the identity permutation yields h_λ. For another permutation σ, put α_i=λ_i−i+σ(i), discard negative terms, and sort its nonnegative entries to a partition ν. For every k, Σ_{i≤k}α_i≥Σ_{i≤k}λ_i, with strictness for some k unless σ=id; sorting only increases prefix sums. Thus ν strictly dominates λ and the Schur-to-h matrix is dominance-unitriangular over Z. Since h_λ is an integral basis, so is s_λ. The Schur Cauchy expansion and the finite dual-kernel criterion for the Hall form then imply self-duality and orthonormality.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: Skew Schur functions by Hall adjointness
items.statement: For partitions λ,μ, set d=|λ|−|μ|. If d<0, define s_{λ/μ}=0; if d≥0, set s_{λ/μ}=Σ_{ν⊢d}⟨s_λ,s_μs_ν⟩s_ν. Equivalently ⟨s_{λ/μ},s_ν⟩=⟨s_λ,s_μs_ν⟩ for every partition ν. No containment criterion is asserted in the definition.
items.proof_strategy: The orthonormal integral Schur basis makes the coefficient prescription finite and unique in each degree; multiplication preserves grading, so negative degree gives zero. Do not assume the later theorem that μ must be contained in λ.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: Skew Jacobi–Trudi and tableau expansion
items.statement: If μ⊆λ, then s_{λ/μ}=det(h_{λ_i−μ_j−i+j})_{1≤i,j≤r}=Σ_T x^{wt(T)}, where r≥max(ℓ(λ),ℓ(μ)) and T ranges over row-weak, column-strict skew tableaux of shape λ/μ. If μ⊈λ, then s_{λ/μ}=0.
items.proof_strategy: From Hall adjointness and Schur Cauchy, derive Σ_λ s_{λ/μ}(x)s_λ(y)=s_μ(y)Ω(x,y). In finitely many y variables multiply by the Vandermonde, expand Ω in h/m form, and compare the coefficient of y^{λ+δ}; this gives the displayed skew determinant. If some λ_r<μ_r, its lower-left rectangular h-zero block forces determinant zero. Apply Cauchy again to split alphabets: s_{λ/μ}(X,Y)=Σ_νs_{λ/ν}(X)s_{ν/μ}(Y). Use the same complementary-minor H/E identity from Jacobi–Trudi to derive the skew dual determinant s_{λ/μ}=det(e_{λ′_i−μ′_j−i+j}); for one variable, this determinant and e_j(t)=0 for j>1 show s_{α/β}(t)=t^{|α|−|β|} exactly for a horizontal strip and zero otherwise. Iterating the split bijects chains of horizontal strips with semistandard skew tableaux, proving the weight sum. Treat empty shapes and negative indices explicitly.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I

items.title: The Kostka change of basis is dominance-unitriangular
items.statement: In each degree d, h_μ=Σ_{λ⊢d}K_{λμ}s_λ. Also K_{λμ}=0 unless λ⊒μ and K_{μμ}=1; the Kostka matrix is therefore integral unitriangular.
items.proof_strategy: Set μ=∅ in the skew tableau expansion and group monomials by exponent partition: s_λ=Σ_νK_{λν}m_ν, using the published Kostka definition. Hall duality gives ⟨s_λ,h_μ⟩=K_{λμ}; Schur orthonormality then yields the displayed h expansion, with labels fixed. In a semistandard tableau, entries at most r can occur only in the first r rows, giving Σ_{i≤r}μ_i≤Σ_{i≤r}λ_i. If shape and weight both equal μ, all these inequalities force row i to consist of i, so K_{μμ}=1. Finite dominance ordering makes the matrix unitriangular.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

title: Symmetric Functions, the Hall Inner Product, and Schur Bases — Examples

items.title: Power sums fail to span integrally in degree two
items.statement: The integral symmetric function h_2=(p_1^2+p_2)/2 cannot be expressed as an integer linear combination of p_{(1,1)} and p_{(2)}.
items.proof_strategy: Expand h_2=m_2+m_{11}, p_1^2=m_2+2m_{11}, and p_2=m_2. An integer combination ap_1^2+bp_2 has even m_{11}-coefficient 2a, whereas h_2 has coefficient one; the displayed rational identity is exact.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: The five standard symmetric-function bases in degree three
items.statement: Write every m, e, h, p and s element in Λ^3 in the ordered monomial basis (m_3,m_{21},m_{111}), with their transition matrices and integral versus rational behavior.
items.proof_strategy: Direct orbit counting gives e_3=m_{111}, e_{21}=m_{21}+3m_{111}, e_{111}=m_3+3m_{21}+6m_{111}; h_3=m_3+m_{21}+m_{111}, h_{21}=m_3+2m_{21}+3m_{111}, h_{111}=m_3+3m_{21}+6m_{111}; p_3=m_3, p_{21}=m_3+m_{21}, p_{111}=m_3+3m_{21}+6m_{111}. Jacobi–Trudi gives s_3=h_3, s_{21}=h_{21}−h_3=m_{21}+2m_{111}, s_{111}=e_3=m_{111}. Put these row vectors into five explicit 3×3 matrices and compare determinants: m,e,h,s are unimodular, p is rational only.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: Cauchy kernel through bidegree three
items.statement: Expand Ω in bidegrees (d,d) for 0≤d≤3 in both complete–monomial and Schur forms, and check that pairing the x-side against s_{21}(x) yields s_{21}(y).
items.proof_strategy: Write Ω_{≤3}=1+h_1m_1+h_2m_2+h_{11}m_{11}+h_3m_3+h_{21}m_{21}+h_{111}m_{111}, with x factors h and y factors m. Compare with Σ_{|λ|≤3}s_λ(x)s_λ(y). Use s_{21}=h_{21}−h_3=m_{21}+2m_{111}; Hall duality gives ⟨s_{21},h_3⟩=0, ⟨s_{21},h_{21}⟩=1, ⟨s_{21},h_{111}⟩=2, so the pairing is m_{21}(y)+2m_{111}(y)=s_{21}(y). Higher bidegrees do not enter.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: A nonzero stable Schur function can vanish in too few variables
items.statement: For every N≥0, s_{(1^{N+1})} is nonzero in Λ but its specialization to N variables is zero.
items.proof_strategy: Dual Jacobi–Trudi gives s_{(1^{N+1})}=e_{N+1}; the Schur integral basis proves the stable element is nonzero. The published finite elementary definition gives e_{N+1}(x_1,…,x_N)=0 since no (N+1)-subset exists; equivalently the fixed-rank alternant has repeated or missing exponents.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9

items.title: A disconnected skew Schur function factors
items.statement: For λ=(3,1), μ=(1), the two edge-disconnected components of λ/μ give s_{(3,1)/(1)}=h_2h_1.
items.proof_strategy: The boxes in row one are columns 2–3 and the row-two box is column 1, with no common edge. The 2×2 skew Jacobi–Trudi matrix is [[h_2,h_4],[h_{−1},h_1]], whose determinant is h_2h_1. Independently, skew tableau fillings of the length-two row and single box are unconstrained across components, so their generating series multiply.

references.title: Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I
Martin, Lecture Notes on Algebraic Combinatorics, Chapter 9
